data.title: Minoxidil 5% solution
data.summary: X Hair & scalp agents · Piperidinopyrimidine derivative; potassium-channel opener (originally an oral antihypertensive)
data.body:
_Topicals · X Hair & scalp agents_

**Class:** Piperidinopyrimidine derivative; potassium-channel opener (originally an oral antihypertensive)

## Mechanism of action
- Prodrug — converted in the hair follicle by sulfotransferase (SULT1A1) to minoxidil sulfate (active)
- Opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels → vasodilation and increased follicle blood flow
- Prolongs anagen, shortens telogen, enlarges miniaturised follicles; stimulates VEGF and dermal papilla cells
- Low follicular sulfotransferase activity predicts poor response

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Androgenetic alopecia — men (5%) and women (2% solution or 5% foam once daily)
- Alopecia areata (adjunct), chemotherapy-induced alopecia (to shorten duration), eyebrow/beard hypotrichosis (off-label)
- Oral low-dose minoxidil (0.25–5 mg/day) — in the Derma Desk 2nd-line ladder

## Dose & formulations
- Men: 1 mL of 5% solution twice daily to dry scalp (affected area), leave at least 4 h; or 5% foam twice daily
- Women: 2% solution 1 mL twice daily or 5% foam once daily
- Shedding in the first 2–8 weeks is expected (telogen release); judge at 6–12 months; must continue — benefit lost in 3–4 months after stopping

## Adverse effects
- Scalp irritation, itching, scaling, contact dermatitis (often due to propylene glycol — foam is PG-free)
- Hypertrichosis of the face/forehead (especially women; from drips or hand transfer)
- Initial shedding; rarely headache, dizziness, palpitations, hypotension (systemic absorption)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity; broken or inflamed scalp
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding; caution in cardiovascular disease

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid in pregnancy (fetal hypertrichosis/malformations reported with systemic exposure) and breastfeeding.

## Viva points
- Prodrug activated by follicular sulfotransferase
- Initial shedding is a sign of response, not failure
- Must be used indefinitely
- Propylene glycol causes most contact dermatitis — switch to foam

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.57 (Miscellaneous topical agents — minoxidil); Khopkar ch.28. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
